definitions.explanation: Describes something intellectually or morally elevated, such as pursuits, tastes, or character. Can also be used ironically to mock pretentiousness.

examples.japanese: {高尚|こうしょう}な{趣味|しゅみ}をお{持|も}ちですね。
examples.english: You have refined tastes, don't you.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{高尚|こうしょう}な{理想|りそう}を{掲|かか}げて{活動|かつどう}している。
examples.english: He is working toward lofty ideals.

examples.japanese: {高尚|こうしょう}な{話題|わだい}ばかりで、{少|すこ}し{堅苦|かたくる}しい{集|あつ}まりだった。
examples.english: It was a somewhat stiff gathering, with nothing but highbrow topics.

notes:
USAGE: {高尚|こうしょう} can be used both sincerely (to praise intellectual or moral refinement) and ironically (to criticize pretentiousness or impracticality). Context determines which reading applies.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {高尚|こうしょう}な{趣味|しゅみ} (refined hobby/taste)
- {高尚|こうしょう}な{人格|じんかく} (noble character)
- {高尚|こうしょう}な{理想|りそう} (lofty ideals)
- {高尚|こうしょう}な{話題|わだい} (highbrow topic)

SIMILAR WORDS: Compare with {上品|じょうひん} (elegant, refined), which focuses on outward manners and appearance, while {高尚|こうしょう} emphasizes intellectual or moral elevation. {崇高|すうこう} (sublime, lofty) is even more elevated and is rarely used ironically.
